---
title: "Understand validation results"
output: html_document
---

Use this guide when reviewing an individual report or an aggregate covering several submitted forms.

## Read the status first

| Status     | Meaning                                                     | Next action                                 |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Valid      | Validation completed without error findings.                 | Review any warnings.                        |
| Invalid    | Validation established a problem that prevents acceptance.   | Review errors and correct the form.          |
| Incomplete | Some checks could not finish. Other findings may also exist. | Resolve unfinished checks and review errors. |
| Failed     | An execution failure prevented successful validation.        | Investigate the failure before rerunning.    |

Passing structure means the form can proceed to later checks; it does not mean the submitted data is valid.

An incomplete result can contain many errors. Follow up both the findings and the unfinished checks.

## Review a collection

Use the status and finding cards to open the relevant detail tab with its filter already applied.

The Warning findings card shows the META handling recorded when the batch was planned.

The Forms table links to individual reports. Model version identifies which definition was used.

Validation findings are grouped by sheet. Select a sheet tab, then filter by field, severity, value or message.

Occurrences count findings; affected forms count submissions. Several findings can come from one form.

Use **Reset filters** to remove the applied filters before reviewing the full table again.

Use the page-size selector for longer lists and **Export CSV** to download the table view.

## Review one form

Use the sheet tabs to find errors and warnings. Detailed findings give the source row and column where available.

Values preserve visible spacing so differences such as trailing spaces can be spotted.

Use the breadcrumb to return to any ancestor aggregate report.

## Follow up unfinished checks

These describe checks that could not complete, such as unavailable references or unresolved rule mappings.

Use the sheet, field and message to identify the affected check. Some failures apply to the whole form.

Send reference or rule problems to the IOTC validation maintainer, with the report and model version.

Send incorrect submitted values to the form provider. A rule problem is not evidence that a submitted value is wrong.

## Use code-list evidence

Open **Code-list evidence** from an aggregate report's Resources section.

Select a rejected value to find affected forms, sheets, fields and source cells.

The Codes CSV summarises rejected values. The Evidence CSV provides locations for follow-up with providers.

Compare the value with the approved list before deciding whether the submission or reference list needs correction.

A rejected value alone does not justify adding a new code. Missing lists and unresolved mappings appear in unfinished checks.

## Use registry evidence

Open **Registry evidence** from an aggregate report's Resources section.

Review errors and warnings for submitted values with no match or multiple matches in a registry.

Select a value to see affected forms, model versions, sheets, fields and exact cell ranges.

The Values CSV summarises cases. The Evidence CSV lists source locations, severity and the reason for review.

Compare each case with the approved registry before changing a form, a registry entry or the matching rules.

Missing registry snapshots and checks that could not finish remain in unfinished checks.

## Review conversion errors

Open **Conversion errors** from an aggregate report's Resources section.

Review rejected values by model version, sheet, field and expected type. Select a value to inspect its source cells.

The report includes number, integer, boolean and temporal type failures, including META warnings.

Values are preserved exactly as recorded. No trimming or coercion is performed, and validation is not rerun.

Use Values CSV for grouped cases and Evidence CSV for affected forms and cells when comparing later batches.

## Download resources

Individual reports provide Summary CSV and Findings CSV downloads.

Aggregate reports provide Forms, Issues and Execution CSV downloads for their scope.

Keep the HTML report with its CSV files and assets when sharing it; a standalone HTML file cannot load the tables.
